title: What a probability guess means
summary: Why 70% means you expect to be wrong 3 times in 10, and why that is fine.

steps.head: A guess with a number
steps.body: In the game you give a {{probability|chance}} that the price will be higher after a few days. A {{guess|guess}} of 70% means you think it is likely, but not sure.

steps.head: What 70% really says
steps.body: Say 70% many times. About 7 of those times the price should go up. About 3 times it should not. Being wrong 3 times in 10 is not a mistake. It is what 70% means.
steps.more: Try the small demo below. Move the slider and look at how many ups you see out of 20.

steps.head: Why not say 100%?
steps.body: A guess of 100% says you can never be wrong. One miss then looks very bad. Honest doubt is part of a good guess.

steps.head: The coin-flip line
steps.body: Saying 50% every time is like flipping a {{coin-flip|coin}}. Your numbers only mean something if they do better than that.

steps.head: Small numbers fool us
steps.body: After three guesses, a lucky run can look like skill. A small {{sample-size|number of guesses}} tells you very little.

questions.prompt: You say 70% on ten different days. About how many times should you be wrong?

options.why: Yes. 70% means you expect to be right about 7 times in 10, so wrong about 3 times.
No. Only a guess of 100% says you are never wrong, and that is rarely wise.
No. That is how often you expect to be right, not wrong.

questions.prompt: You said 70% and the price fell. Was that a bad guess?

options.text: Not by itself. One miss is normal.
options.why: Right. A 70% guess should miss about 3 times in 10. Judge guesses over many days.

options.text: Yes. The price should have risen.
options.why: Not so. A guess of 70% never says the price must rise.
No. A guess of 100% would have been far worse after this miss.

questions.prompt: What does it mean to say 50% every time?

options.text: You have no view. It is the same as a coin flip.
options.why: Right. A fixed 50% is the line your real guesses need to improve on.
No. A fixed 50% is right about half the time.
No. It is right about half the time, like a coin.
